Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 7 Part IV reduction, zero when the dotted line is blank

Fact.Name: Qualified disaster distribution is inside the statutory 180-day window

The test is written as receipt date minus 180 days, less than the applicable date: the same boundary, expressed in the engine's calendar arithmetic, so leap days, year crossings and a receipt year EARLIER than a later declaration year are all handled by the calendar rather than by day-of-year ordinals. A blank date is never read as a disqualification: a distribution that is not a qualified disaster distribution is fully taxable and exposed to the section 72(t) additional tax, and that is not a conclusion a missing answer may reach. Fact.Name: The other-than-IRA qualified amount this year's ordinary pension route must NOT carry
Fact.Description:
The taxable part of this year's other-than-IRA qualified disaster distributions — Form 8915-F line 10, line 8 less the applicable cost on line 9 — which Part II taxes over three years and which therefore may not ALSO reach Form 1040 line 5b through the ordinary Form 1099-R route.
WHY THE PRINTED FORM SETTLES THE DIRECTION. Line 7 says "Enter the EXCESS of the sum of lines 2 through 4 in column (a) over the amount on line 6. The excess, and only the excess, is what the ordinary route reports; the line 6 qualified amount leaves that route entirely and is taxed through Parts II and III instead. The ordinary route carries the Form 1099-R box 2a TAXABLE amount, so what has to come out of it is the taxable part of the qualified amount, which is line 10 and not the line 2 column (b) gross — line 9 is exactly the cost the printed form allocates to the qualified portion, and subtracting the gross would remove basis the ordinary route never included.
WHY AN EXCLUSION TERM IS NEEDED. One might think form1099Rs:/flowKnockoutRetirementQualifiedDisasterDistribution refuses every return carrying a current-year qualified disaster distribution, so that no exclusion term is needed on /form8915FLine15AmountSubjectToTaxOrZero or income:/taxableIraDistributions. Fact.Name: This Form 8915-F reports the spouse, not the primary taxpayer
Fact.Description:
WHOSE Form 8915-F this is, on a joint return. FALSE (or absent) means the primary taxpayer's; TRUE means the spouse's.
WHY THIS IS AN INTAKE AND NOT AN INFERENCE. Form 8915-F is a PER-PERSON form and the printed form says so twice. "Married filers. If both you and your spouse are required to file Form 8915-F, file a separate Form 8915-F for each of you" - so one Form 8915-F is one person's, never a household's. And the form has a box that answers this question already: "Name and social security number (SSN). If you file a joint return, enter only the name and SSN of the SPOUSE WHOSE INFORMATION IS BEING REPORTED on the Form 8915-F." This writable is that box. It is not a new question invented to make a computation work; it is a printed identification field this dictionary had no fact for.
WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not the whole of the gap. This dictionary holds ONE return-level Form 8915-F, so a joint return where BOTH spouses have qualified disaster distributions still needs a second form and a second printed instance, and that remains unbuilt and named as a residual. What this writable buys is the case that is both commoner and wrong today: ONE Form 8915-F on a joint return, whose waiver was being spent against the primary filer whoever actually received the distribution.
A BOOLEAN RATHER THAN A FILER POINTER, deliberately. On a joint return there are exactly two candidates and the printed field names one of them; a pointer would admit a third answer the form does not have. The per-item filer pointers in form1099Rs are a different shape for a different reason - they hang off a COLLECTION, where the roster is the only way to say which item is whose.

Fact.Name: This Form 8915-F is the primary taxpayer's
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the return holds a Form 8915-F and it is the primary taxpayer's. FALSE when the return holds no Form 8915-F at all. INCOMPLETE, deliberately, on a two-member roster whose ownership answer is blank.
THE CASE ORDER IS THE WHOLE DESIGN, and it is what keeps this fact from repeating an earlier guard-ordering failure. Read it in order:
(1) NO FORM, NO OWNER. A return that has answered no Form 8915-F intake resolves FALSE here without consulting the roster or the ownership answer. Every return in the committed corpus that files no Form 8915-F therefore takes this branch, and nothing downstream of it can go Incomplete.
(2) A ONE-MEMBER ROSTER OWNS IT. Tested as Not IsComplete(filers:/secondaryFiler), NOT as "the filing status is not MFJ". filers:/secondaryFiler is a Find over /filers and resolves INCOMPLETE on a one-member roster, which is precisely the signal wanted, and it works on a fixture whose filing status is unanswered - where a read of filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ would itself be Incomplete and take the fact off the end of the Switch. That distinction is the same failure in miniature: a guard that is UNDECIDED on a minimal fixture is not the same as a guard that is false.
(3) THE ANSWER, WHEN THERE IS ONE.
AND THEN NOTHING. There is no True catch-all, and its absence is the point rather than an omission: a joint return holding a Form 8915-F whose owner nobody has stated cannot be attributed by this graph, and a default here would spend a spouse's waiver against the wrong person's line 1 silently. That Incomplete is REACHED only through form5329's waiver-share facts, which test for a positive waiver FIRST - so a joint return with a Form 8915-F but no qualified disaster distribution never asks the question.

Fact.Name: This Form 8915-F is the spouse's
Fact.Description: The twin of /form8915FBelongsToPrimaryFiler and case-for-case identical to it except that a one-member roster resolves FALSE here rather than TRUE: a return with no spouse has no spouse's form. The same absent True catch-all, for the same reason, and the same Incomplete on a two-member roster whose ownership answer is blank.

Fact.Name: The name printed at the top of Form 8915-F: the owner's, not the household's
Fact.Description:
The PRINTED half. The Name box at the top of page 1. Before this fact the register bound that box to filers:/primaryFiler/fullName unconditionally, so a Form 8915-F reporting the SPOUSE'S qualified disaster distribution printed the PRIMARY taxpayer's name beside it - an identity error on a filed form, attributing the distribution to someone who never received it. The instruction is explicit: "If you file a joint return, enter only the name and SSN of the spouse whose information is being reported on the Form 8915-F", and the printed caption over the box says the same ("If married, file a separate form for each spouse").
INCOMPLETE WHEN THE OWNER IS UNKNOWN, and that is the correct answer rather than a gap. A name box that cannot be filled truthfully must stay blank rather than print a guess; a default here would print a fabricated attribution. It inherits its completeness from /form8915FBelongsToPrimaryFiler and /form8915FBelongsToSecondaryFiler, so it is Incomplete exactly when a joint return holds a Form 8915-F and nobody has said whose it is - and on a one-member roster it is the primary's name, Complete, with no question asked.

Fact.Name: The SSN printed at the top of Form 8915-F: the owner's, not the household's
Fact.Description: The twin of /form8915FOwnerFullName for the SSN box, and the more consequential of the two: the SSN is what the IRS matches on. Same cases, same Incomplete when the owner is unknown, same reason - an SSN box that cannot be filled truthfully is left unresolved rather than filled with the primary taxpayer's number by default.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 26 income less repayment before the zero floor
Fact.Description: line 24 less line 25, the Part III income for this year after the repayments, before the form floors it at zero. The Part III twin of /form8915FLine15IncomeLessRepayment.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 27 No box
Fact.Description: the No box on line 27 of Form 8915-F: no Part IV qualified distribution has to be reported on this year's Form 8606, so the form goes to line 28. The twin of the line 27 Yes box, and blank like it until the filer answers.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 28 or zero
Fact.Description: line 28, the Part IV qualified distributions for a main-home purchase or construction. When dated item records exist, this is the sum of only in-window item amounts; an out-of-window item contributes zero and an item with unanswered date evidence leaves treatment Incomplete. Without dated items, the established aggregate input remains authoritative and a blank line reads as zero.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 29 or zero
Fact.Description: line 29 read as zero when the filer left it blank, so line 30 still resolves for a Part IV qualified distribution with no cost basis.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 30 Part IV distributions after the applicable cost
Fact.Description: line 30 of Form 8915-F: line 28 less line 29, the Part IV qualified distributions after the return of the filer's investment in the contract and before the repayments on line 31.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 31 or zero
Fact.Description: line 31 read as zero when the filer left it blank, so line 32 still resolves for a filer who repaid nothing.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 32 taxable amount of the Part IV qualified distributions
Fact.Description: line 32 of Form 8915-F: line 30 less line 31, the taxable amount of the qualified distributions the filer received for the purchase or construction of a main home in a disaster area and did not repay. Line 32 carries no zero floor: the form prints the subtraction as it falls. PRINT ONLY until the rewire below lands.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 3 column (b) is more than zero
Fact.Description: true when the filer entered a traditional IRA qualified disaster distribution on line 3, column (b). One half of the line 16 question.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 3 column (b) or zero
Fact.Description: line 3, column (b), the traditional-IRA qualified disaster distributions. Dated item records govern when present: only in-window item amounts are included, outside-window items contribute zero, and unanswered date evidence remains Incomplete. Otherwise the established aggregate input is retained, blank as zero.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 4 column (b) is more than zero
Fact.Description: true when the filer entered a Roth IRA qualified disaster distribution on line 4, column (b). The other half of the line 16 question.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 4 column (b) or zero
Fact.Description: line 4, column (b), the Roth-IRA qualified disaster distributions. Dated item records govern when present: only in-window item amounts are included, outside-window items contribute zero, and unanswered date evidence remains Incomplete. Otherwise the established aggregate input is retained, blank as zero.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 9 or zero
Fact.Description: line 9 read as zero when the filer left it blank, so line 10 and every Part II line below it still resolve for a filer whose qualified disaster distribution has no cost basis.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F Part IV Disaster Table rows
Fact.Description: the disasters of /form8915FDisasters for which the filer reports qualified distributions for the purchase or construction of a main home in Part IV, one item per printed row of the Part IV Disaster Table. The table prints two rows over the FEMA number, declaration date, beginning date and ending date columns.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F election not to spread the taxable amount over 3 years
Fact.Description: the election box printed on line 11 and again on line 22 of Form 8915-F: the filer elects NOT to spread the taxable amount of the qualified disaster distributions over 3 years and to include all of it in income this year. One Bool fills both printed boxes because the form requires them to be checked together: line 11 says to check its box if the line 22 box is checked and line 22 says the same of line 11. FILER SUPPLIED: the election is a taxpayer choice no return document carries.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 12 income for prior years from other than IRA qualified disaster distributions
Fact.Description: line 12 of Form 8915-F: the amount from Worksheet 2 in the instructions, this year's one third instalment of qualified disaster distributions the filer received in a prior year and spread over 3 years. FILER SUPPLIED: it is prior year return knowledge, and the graph holds no earlier Form 8915-F.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 14 total repayment of other than IRA qualified disaster distributions
Fact.Description: line 14 of Form 8915-F: the amount from Worksheet 3, the total the filer repaid this year of the other than IRA qualified disaster distributions. A repayment made within the 3 year window is treated as a rollover and reduces the income otherwise reported. FILER SUPPLIED: a recontribution to a plan is not on any document the graph reads.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 17 Yes box
Fact.Description: the Yes box on line 17 of Form 8915-F: the filer received a qualified disaster distribution from an IRA that this year's Form 8606 must report, so lines 18 and 19 carry the Form 8606 amounts. FILER SUPPLIED: the graph's Form 8606 facts model lines 15b and 25b as structurally zero, so nothing in the graph knows that a distribution is both a qualified disaster distribution and a Form 8606 line.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 18 Form 8606 line 15b amount
Fact.Description: line 18 of Form 8915-F: the amount on this year's Form 8606, line 15b, that is attributable to the qualified disaster distributions of this Form 8915-F. FILER SUPPLIED, and now load-bearing on both sides: form8606:/form8606Line15b READS this fact, so Form 8606 line 15c is reduced by it and the qualified disaster amount reaches Form 1040 line 4b once, through line 26 of this form. The figure itself stays the filer's, for two reasons no graph fact can supply: i8606's Line 15b fraction needs a per-distribution qualified disaster amount, and the per form attribution across several Forms 8915-F is knowledge this dictionary does not hold.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 19 Form 8606 line 25b amount
Fact.Description: line 19 of Form 8915-F: the amount on this year's Form 8606, line 25b, that is attributable to the qualified disaster distributions of this Form 8915-F, the Roth IRA counterpart of line 18. FILER SUPPLIED for the same reasons as line 18, and read by form8606:/form8606Line25b, so Form 8606 line 25c is reduced by it. Its fraction's denominator is Form 8606 line 21, not line 19.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 20 traditional IRA qualified disaster distributions not reported on Form 8606
Fact.Description: the part of line 3, column (b) that this year's Form 8606 does not report, which is what line 20 prints when the filer answered Yes on line 17. FILER SUPPLIED: only the filer knows which of the traditional IRA qualified disaster distributions the Form 8606 already carried on line 15b.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 23 income for prior years from IRA qualified disaster distributions
Fact.Description: line 23 of Form 8915-F: the amount from Worksheet 4 in the instructions, this year's one third instalment of IRA qualified disaster distributions the filer received in a prior year. FILER SUPPLIED prior year return knowledge, like its Part II twin on line 12.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 25 total repayment of IRA qualified disaster distributions
Fact.Description: line 25 of Form 8915-F: the amount from Worksheet 5, the total the filer repaid this year of the IRA qualified disaster distributions. A recontribution to an IRA within the 3 year window is treated as a section 408(d)(3) rollover. FILER SUPPLIED, like its Part II twin on line 14.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 27 Yes box
Fact.Description: the Yes box on line 27 of Form 8915-F: the filer received a qualified distribution for the purchase or construction of a main home in a Part IV Disaster Table area that is from an IRA and that this year's Form 8606 must report. A Yes stops Part IV unless the filer also had qualified distributions the Form 8606 does not report. FILER SUPPLIED: nothing in the graph classifies a distribution as a home purchase qualified distribution.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 28 qualified distributions for the purchase or construction of a main home
Fact.Description: line 28 of Form 8915-F: the total the filer received this year of qualified distributions for the purchase or construction of a main home in the area of a Part IV Disaster Table disaster, excluding anything reported on this year's Form 8606 and anything already reported on line 8 or line 20 or on another Form 8915. FILER SUPPLIED: the graph has no first time homebuyer distribution classification at all.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 29 applicable cost of the Part IV qualified distributions
Fact.Description: line 29 of Form 8915-F: the applicable cost of the qualified distributions on line 28, the part of them that is a return of the filer's investment in the contract. FILER SUPPLIED, like its Part II twin on line 9.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 31 repayments of the Part IV qualified distributions
Fact.Description: line 31 of Form 8915-F: the total the filer repaid of the qualified distributions on line 28, excluding any repayment treated as a rollover on this year's Form 8606. A repayment made during the qualified distribution repayment period is a contribution to an eligible retirement plan under the recontribution rule. FILER SUPPLIED: a recontribution is on no document the graph reads. THE SAME REPAYMENT IS ALSO ENTERED ON THE FORM 1099-R THAT REPORTED THE DISTRIBUTION, as that form's indirect rollover (form1099Rs:/form1099Rs/*/writableIsIndirectRollover yes, its amount in form1099RFrontier:/form1099Rs/*/writableIndirectRolloverAmount, and the rollover period that applies answered yes). A repayment made during the qualified distribution repayment period is treated as a trustee-to-trustee transfer and is not included in income, and the item's rollover exclusion is what takes it out of the item's taxable amount - so out of Form 1040 line 4b or 5b and out of Form 5329 line 1, whose Form 1099-R part is each early distribution's includible amount. This line is printed and caps the attested Form 5329 line 32 route; it does not itself reduce any Form 1099-R amount, because nothing ties it to the document that carried the distribution. A line 31 amount larger than the rollovers entered on the Forms 1099-R, on a return with an early-coded Form 1099-R, is refused (form5329:/knockoutForm8915FLine31RepaymentNotOnItsForm1099R) while the Part IV distribution is carried on those forms.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 9 applicable cost of the other than IRA distributions
Fact.Description: line 9 of Form 8915-F: the applicable cost of the qualified disaster distributions on line 8, the part of those distributions that is a return of the filer's investment in the contract and so is not taxable. FILER SUPPLIED: box 5 of a Form 1099-R carries employee contributions only when the payer computed the taxable amount, and the graph holds no basis recovery for a qualified disaster distribution.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F dates of qualified distributions received this year
Fact.Description: the free text line above line 27 naming the date or dates on which the filer received the qualified distributions for the purchase or construction of a main home reported in Part IV. The printed caption is plural and one box carries every date, so this intake is a String and not a Day. FILER SUPPLIED: no return document carries the date of a retirement distribution. PRINT ONLY as one line until the obligation below is met.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F was answered (the filer opened the form)
Fact.Description:
THE RENDER GATE for Form 8915-F, an ANSWERED-NESS predicate in the shape form1116:/form1116Answered set. The printed rule is a list of four circumstances — "File Form 8915-F for the year you checked in item A at the top of page 1 of the form if any of the following apply to you for that year for the disasters listed in items C and D: A qualified disaster distribution was made to you from an eligible retirement plan; You received a qualified distribution; A qualified disaster distribution was made to you in a prior year that you are including in income in equal amounts over 3 years and 'this year' is a year within the 3-year period; You made a repayment of a qualified disaster distribution and the time for filing the Form 8915-F for that repayment has not expired" — and each of the four has an intake here: the item C disaster list (/form8915FDisasters) and the item D qualified distributions (/form8915FQualifiedDistributions), which together carry the first two bullets; the prior-year income spread over three years, Part I line 12 and Part IV line 23; a repayment, Part I line 14, Part IV line 25 and line 31; and every other root dollar intake this module owns — the line 1a-1e limit inputs, the column (a) and column (b) amounts on lines 2 through 5a, the Form 8606 attributions on lines 18 through 20, and the Part IV lines 28 and 29 — together with the Form 8606 and coronavirus indications. A filer who has answered any one of the DOLLAR intakes has opened this form; the two Form 8606 indications and the coronavirus indication are read as values, so only a TRUE on one of them opens it.
AN INPUT TEST, NOT A VALUE TEST, and deliberately. A repayment year with no current-year distribution has $0 on every taxable line and still files the form; and /form8915FQualifiedDistributions/*/qddWindowIsSatisfied is INCOMPLETE on an item whose qualified-disaster-distribution dates are unanswered, so any value-based Any over the Part I / Part IV "has qualified distributions" facts would inherit that Incomplete on the form-opened-but-dates-blank return — which is precisely the return a render gate must still answer for. IsComplete resolves Complete on every return, so this predicate is complete-safe by construction, and that is what lets the Part II and Part III wrappers use it as the gate under which an Incomplete line 15 or line 26 may reach Form 1040.
AN EMPTY BUT CREATED COLLECTION READS AS NOT ANSWERED. js/src/setupFactGraph.ts seeds an EMPTY collection for every writable Collection fact on a return that persists no /filers, so a bare IsComplete over the item C disaster list or the item D qualified distributions is TRUE on a return that opened nothing, and this gate would print Form 8915-F on every such return. Both collection legs are therefore a PRESENCE test inside an IsComplete guard — qbi:/qbiHasPatronBusiness's idiom: an absent collection resolves Complete FALSE, an answered-but-empty one FALSE, a table with one row TRUE. The scalar legs are untouched, because IsComplete on an unanswered scalar writable is Complete FALSE already.
ANSWERED-NESS IS NOT ELIGIBILITY, completeness, approval to file, or a promise that the application emits a separate form for a spouse or for another disaster year.

Fact.Name: Incident-period ending date for an itemized Part IV distribution
Fact.Description:
the last day of the incident period for this item's qualified disaster. This is the inclusive upper anchor of the Part IV receipt window: a qualified distribution for the purchase or construction of a main home must be received no earlier than 180 days before the first day of the incident period and no later than 30 days after its last day.
ASK: "When did this disaster's incident period end?" HELP: use the incident-period ENDING date FEMA published for the same disaster whose beginning date you gave above — not the date the disaster was declared, which is a different date and is usually later. ASKED WHEN: this qualified-distribution item carries a Part IV home-purchase amount above zero. UNANSWERED: the item's Part IV window, and with it the Part IV qualified amount, is Incomplete; a blank date never disqualifies the distribution. VALIDATION: a Day, on or after the incident-period beginning date; an ending date before the beginning date is refused. FEEDS: ../part4WindowIsSatisfied, and through it Form 8915-F line 28 and Part IV.
IT HAS A PRINTED TWIN AND IS NOT IT. /form8915FDisasters/*/writableDisasterEndingDate is the same FEMA date on the item C disaster collection, and it is the one that prints, in the Disaster ending date column of the Part IV Disaster Table on page 4. This one computes and does not print. The two collections have no derivation between them — the same is true of this collection's beginning and declaration dates — so the application must carry one answer to both and must not raise two questions. Deriving the per-distribution dates from the disaster row the item belongs to needs a disaster-to-distribution link this module does not hold, and that link is the named successor.

Fact.Name: Part IV receipt window for qualified 2021 and later disasters
Fact.Description:
TRUE only when this item's typed receipt date falls in the Part IV window: no earlier than 180 days before the first day of the incident period and no later than 30 days after its last day, both boundaries inclusive. The incident period must itself begin on or after January 26, 2021 — the floor the instructions set for a qualified 2021 disaster, and a test every later disaster passes by its own date. An item with any unanswered date matches no case and resolves INCOMPLETE, and so does an item whose incident period ENDS BEFORE IT BEGINS: two answered dates that contradict each other are a data fault for the filer to correct, not a finding that the distribution fails the window, and a FALSE here would zero line 28 from a typo.
THIS IS THE RECEIPT-DATE PREDICATE ONLY. That the distribution was a hardship distribution from a 401(k) plan or a tax-sheltered annuity, or a qualified first-time homebuyer distribution from an IRA; that it was to be used to buy or build a main home in the disaster's qualified disaster area; and that the home was not bought or built because of the disaster are all taxpayer evidence this graph does not hold. The separate period for REPAYING a qualified distribution is a different interval and is not tested here, and the special Part IV route for a 2020 disaster is not implemented.

Fact.Name: Sum of Form 8915-F column-(b) allocations
Fact.Description: the sum of the Form 8915-F line 2, line 3 and line 4 column (b) amounts. It is an allocation checksum read by /form8915FPart1AllocationIsValid and nothing else: it adds no income, it applies no per-disaster cap, and it prints on no line.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F Part I category allocation is consistent
Fact.Description:
TRUE only when the Part I category allocation is internally consistent with what the printed form requires of it: the line 2, 3 and 4 column (b) amounts add to line 5b column (b) (which is line 6); each of them is at most its own column (a) amount; their sum is at most the distributions available for qualified treatment; line 5a is at most the line 2 through line 4 column (a) total; no term is negative; and the dollar limit the allocation is capped by is itself consistent, which is /form8915FLine1eLimitIsConsistent — a line 1e above the sum of lines 1c and 1d that the filer's own lines 1a, 1b and 1d determine would otherwise let this predicate certify an allocation against a limit the printed form does not allow. Two facts carry that last conjunct: /form8915FLine1eLimitIsConsistent tests line 1e against the filer's own lines 1c and 1d, and /form8915FLine1ePerDisasterCapIsRespected tests it against the per disaster dollar limit times the number of rows in the Part I Disaster Table.
WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT A REBALANCE. The form tells the filer to allocate the column (b) amounts "by any reasonable method" so that they total line 5b column (b). Which reasonable method is chosen decides how much of the qualified amount is traditional-IRA money and how much is Roth money, and that moves IRA basis and Form 8606 treatment. It is the filer's choice, not a derivation, so an allocation that does not total line 6 — including one the line 1e dollar limit has capped — resolves FALSE and Parts II and III stay Incomplete until the filer corrects it. Nothing is silently reassigned and no cap is silently applied. An unresolved operand leaves this fact Incomplete rather than FALSE, so a missing answer never reads as a contradiction.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 1e agrees with the printed sum of lines 1c and 1d
Fact.Description:
TRUE unless the filer completed lines 1a, 1b and 1d and then entered a line 1e larger than the sum of lines 1c and 1d that those three lines determine.
WHY THE TEST IS CONDITIONAL. The printed form has two routes to line 1e. The common filer is sent straight to line 1e and told to leave lines 1a through 1d blank, and a Worksheet 1B filer leaves 1a through 1e blank; on either route there is nothing to compare, so this fact is TRUE and the limit the filer supplied is taken as given. The other instruction bullet is the one this fact enforces: where lines 1a through 1d ARE answered, line 1e is their arithmetic consequence, and an entry above it is not a choice the form offers. Line 1e caps line 5b column (b), which is line 6, which is both the amount whose section 72(t) additional tax is waived and the amount Parts II and III spread over three years, so an overstated line 1e understates this year's Form 1040 lines 4b and 5b.
WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT A CAP, AND WHY ONLY THE OVERSTATEMENT. /form8915FLine1eAvailableLimitOrZero is not rewritten and the printed line 1e cell still carries the filer's own answer, so the printed form and the computed form cannot disagree. Instead this fact joins /form8915FPart1AllocationIsValid, and an inconsistent limit therefore leaves Parts II and III Incomplete until the filer corrects line 1e. The test is one-sided: an entry BELOW the sum only costs the filer qualified treatment they were entitled to, and that is not a number this graph will refuse to file. An unanswered operand leaves the comparison unreached and the fact TRUE, never FALSE, so a missing answer never reads as a contradiction. This is also what gives /form8915FLine1cRemainingLimit its first arithmetic consumer; before this fact it was printed and thrown away.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F item B names calendar year 2020
Fact.Description: whether the item B box the filer checked is the 2020 box, read complete safely: TRUE only where the 2020 box is answered TRUE, and FALSE on every other return, including one that has answered no item B box at all. Item B names the single calendar year in which every qualified disaster on this Form 8915-F began, and the printed line 1d cell gives that year its own per disaster figure, so this fact is the selector between the two printed limits and is read for nothing else. It is the first consumer any item B box has ever had.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F per disaster qualified disaster distribution limit
Fact.Description: the dollar figure the printed line 1d cell multiplies by a count of qualified disasters: 22,000 dollars, or 100,000 dollars where item B names 2020. It is the section 72(t)(11)(B)(i) aggregate limit for ONE qualified disaster. The form prints both figures in the same cell because item B fixes a single disaster year for the whole form, so exactly one of them applies to every Form 8915-F and no return can need both.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F aggregate per disaster limit for the Part I Disaster Table
Fact.Description: the per disaster limit times the number of rows in the Part I Disaster Table, which is the largest amount of qualified disaster distributions the statute allows for the disasters this form reports. The printed line 1d cell performs exactly this multiplication for the disasters that are NEW this year; the same arithmetic over every row of the table is the ceiling line 1e cannot exceed, because line 1e is line 1c plus line 1d and line 1c is what remains of the same per disaster figure after the prior year distributions on line 1b. A table with no rows gives zero dollars here, which is why the consumer below reads this fact only where the table has at least one row: a return that lists no disaster is not bounded by a zero.

Fact.Name: Form 8915-F line 1e is within the per disaster limit for the disasters listed in Part I
Fact.Description:
TRUE unless the filer listed at least one disaster in the Part I Disaster Table and then entered a line 1e above the per disaster limit times the number of listed rows.
WHY THE TABLE SIZE IS THE KEY, AND WHY A SIZE OF ZERO BUYS NO BOUND. The printed line 1d cell multiplies the per disaster figure by a COUNT of qualified disasters, so a count is the form's own unit of measure for this limit, and the Part I Disaster Table is where the form counts the disasters whose distributions Part I reports. A return that answers line 1e and lists no table row has not told this graph how many disasters the limit is claimed for, and a ceiling of zero dollars would refuse it outright; the guard therefore requires a table with at least one row before any comparison is made, and every return that answers line 1e with no table resolves exactly as it did before this fact existed. That population is not marginal: it is most of the returns in this module's own fixtures.
WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT A CAP, AND WHY ONLY THE OVERSTATEMENT. The shape is /form8915FLine1eLimitIsConsistent's and the reasons are the same: /form8915FLine1eAvailableLimitOrZero is not rewritten, so the printed line 1e cell keeps the filer's own answer and print cannot disagree with compute; the refusal travels through /form8915FPart1AllocationIsValid, leaving Parts II and III Incomplete until the filer corrects line 1e. An entry BELOW the ceiling costs the filer only qualified treatment they were entitled to and is not refused. An unanswered line 1e, an unanswered disaster list, or a table row whose Part I flag is blank leaves the comparison unreached and this fact TRUE, never FALSE, so a missing answer never reads as a contradiction.

Fact.Name: A Part II or Part III line the form cannot figure from the answers given
Fact.Description: TRUE when line 9, the cost of the line 8 distributions, is more than line 8; or line 18 plus line 20 is more than line 3 column (b); or line 19 is more than line 4 column (b). These are the exact negations of the extra conditions /form8915FLine10TaxableAmount and /form8915FLine21TaxableAmount require, so on these answers lines 10 and 21 stay Incomplete. Each leg speaks only where the form reaches its lines: Part II only when line 2 column (b) is more than $0 (line 8 otherwise says skip lines 8 through 11), Part III only when line 3 or line 4 column (b) is more than $0 (line 16 otherwise says skip lines 17 through 22). FALSE, never Incomplete, while any operand is unresolved.

Fact.Name: Knockout when a Form 8915-F the filer opened has an inconsistent Part I
Fact.Description:
Refuses a return that opened Form 8915-F and whose Part I entries contradict the printed form, which is /form8915FPart1AllocationIsValid resolved FALSE: a column (b) allocation that does not total line 5b column (b), a column (b) amount above its own column (a), a negative term, a line 1e above the sum of lines 1c and 1d, or a line 1e above the per disaster limit for the disasters listed in the Part I Disaster Table. It also refuses, with Part I valid, a line 9 cost above line 8 (line 10 is line 8 less line 9, the cost of those same distributions), and a line 18 plus line 20 above line 3 column (b) or a line 19 above line 4 column (b) (lines 18 and 19 are the Form 8606 taxable parts of those column (b) distributions and line 20 is the rest of line 3 column (b)): the same inputs on which /form8915FLine10TaxableAmount and /form8915FLine21TaxableAmount stay Incomplete, so the refusal is stated instead of silent.
WHY THIS FACT EXISTS. The refusal was already there and the filer could not see it. /form8915FLine10TaxableAmount and /form8915FLine21TaxableAmount are single-Case Switches with no default arm, so a FALSE allocation leaves them Incomplete, and that Incomplete reaches lines 15 and 26 and then /taxablePensionsAndAnnuities. What the filer gets is a Form 1040 with lines 4b and 5b blank and nothing anywhere saying why, which is the worst of both worlds: the return neither computes nor refuses out loud. This fact is the carrier that makes the same refusal VISIBLE, and it changes no number: everything downstream of the allocation predicate was already Incomplete on exactly this population.
COMPLETE SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, and it has to be, because /flowIsKnockedOut is an Any that every return evaluates. /form8915FPart1AllocationIsValid is Incomplete whenever one of its own twelve operands is unresolved, so it is read behind an IsComplete guard and the default arm supplies a Complete FALSE. A return that opened a Form 8915-F whose Part I dates or amounts are still unresolved is therefore NOT refused here: the Incomplete-propagation channel is still what stops that return, and this carrier speaks only where the graph has actually resolved the contradiction.
WHY ANSWERED-NESS IS NOT RE-TESTED, stated because its absence is the obvious objection.
